summary.text: Liz Brown is a Republican Indiana state senator who has represented District 15 since November 2014 and is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot for re-election.
She is a mediator and attorney who chairs the Senate Judiciary Committee.

paragraphs.text: Brown earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Notre Dame and a law degree from the University of Iowa College of Law in 1983, according to Ballotpedia.
Her career experience includes working as a mediator and attorney, and she previously served on the Fort Wayne City Council and the Fort Wayne City Plan Commission.
Brown assumed office in the state Senate on November 5, 2014.
For the 2025-2026 session she chairs the Senate Judiciary Committee and is also assigned to the Appropriations, Corrections and Criminal Law, Ethics, and Health and Provider Services committees.
In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as having been married for more than four decades and as the mother of seven children with her husband, Dr. Steve Brown.

She listed her campaign priorities in that survey as keeping Indiana affordable through zero-based state budgets and fiscal restraint, immigration enforcement and national security legislation, and more accessible health care.
